hook: SCP-3388 is an 8.5 cm moon cactus that can move anything within seven meters with enormous force. Read the footnote on moon cacti before the text messages, because the way these houseplants are made is the key to the whole joke. There are three deaths in this file, and one body is found missing several bones.
whyItMatters:
The article mixes a bodycam horror log with a comedy of misplaced power. The scary part is short and clinical; the payoff is in the garbled text messages, where two very different voices share one phone number.

It also shows how much an SCP can do with formatting alone. Words from one speaker cut into the middle of another's sentences, and untangling them is half the fun.
thingsToNotice:
The messages come from two beings fused by grafting: a pompous self-proclaimed Elder God called Carnegias, and the small cactus it was grafted onto, which writes in lowercase. The power went to the wrong half, so the god cannot even move, while the plain little plant, wanting rocks and water, killed its owners and took their bones as its rocks, then drained Agent Andrews as the saucepan filled. Its lowercase lines are just needs and feelings: the soil is soggy, it is thirsty, there is now too much water.

When Carnegias tells it that its owners are dead because of what it did, the cactus answers that it is sad, and the god admits he is too. In the messages to Agent Tennison the plant apologizes for hurting people and asks for forgiveness, then Carnegias offers to teach it how to give someone an endless nightmare and it agrees, bidding Tennison farewell in the god's own style. The last line merges them for good, with Carnegias correcting the plant's boast to say that they are a smart cactus together.
